headline: Brady Warns CJGJ as Allen Defends New Uniforms
writeup: Buffalo Bills training camp 2026 opened in Pittsford under rainy skies but electric energy, with Bills Mafia turning out in force to greet a franchise that feels genuinely transformed under first-year head coach Joe Brady — a new voice who wasted no time making his presence felt, reportedly warning safety CJ Gardner-Johnson about locker room behavior after shutting down an unauthorized livestream, a move that signaled Brady's no-nonsense approach from day one. On the field, Josh Allen and newly acquired wide receiver DJ Moore wasted no time building chemistry, with Moore making a highlight-reel grab early in practice while Keon Coleman delivered an up-and-down debut that nonetheless drew public confidence from Allen and GM Brandon Beane, who called Coleman's maturity a work in progress but remained committed to the third-year wideout heading into what many are calling a pivotal season. The injury front brought some concern, with Tyrell Shavers opening camp on the PUP list following an ACL injury and another unnamed wideout absent after a failed physical, while Beane reinforced that there's no rushing the roster-building process of training camp as he addressed a packed media contingent eager for updates on the 53-man puzzle. Off the field, the Bills unveiled their new 'Nickel City' alternate uniforms ahead of the inaugural season at Highmark Stadium — a reveal that drew mixed reactions from fans and prompted Allen to passionately defend the jerseys, urging critics to 'stop hating,' while towering illuminated bison statues at the new stadium added to the sense that a new era in Buffalo has truly arrived. New partnerships with Utica National Insurance and Palmer Food Services, bullish Super Bowl odds from major outlets, and a fanbase buzzing with belief all underscored the feeling that the 2026 Bills are carrying the weight — and the hope — of a city ready to finally see Josh Allen hoist the Lombardi Trophy.
